title: Telemetry data guardrails: tenant-aware redaction, adaptive retention, and access logging for traces & metrics
creator: Aisha Kapur
description:
Summary:
We need a tenant-aware telemetry governance layer that enforces PII suppression, adaptive retention windows, and comprehensive access logging for tracing and metric/log pipelines. This ticket covers design and implementation of redaction hooks at the tracing ingestion layer, retention policy enforcement in the metric/log pipeline, and RBAC-bound access logging for queries and exports.

Background / Problem:
Currently traces and high-cardinality metrics can contain user identifiers and sensitive metadata (email, phone, SSN-like tokens, unredacted URLs). Retention is global and coarse-grained, leading to unnecessarily long storage for telemetry from non-critical tenants. Access to raw telemetry is not consistently logged with tenant-scoped audit trails, creating compliance gaps for SOC2/GDPR.

Goals:
- Implement deterministic PII suppression in trace and span attributes via pluggable trace-hooks before persistence.
- Enforce tenant-scoped retention policy configuration with default tiers (short/medium/long) and an override flow for enterprise tenants.
- Emit access logs for any read/export of raw telemetry, tied to RBAC principals and tenant context.
- Ensure observability (metrics/dashboards) for redaction efficacy, retention enforcement, and access-log volume.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include full schema migration for time-series indices or cold-storage tiering; those will be separate follow-ups.

Acceptance criteria (must pass QA):
1) New trace-hook library applied in the ingestion path that strips or hashes attributes matching configured patterns (regex for emails, phone, SSN-like patterns, jwt tokens in headers).
2) Admin Console UI + API to set tenant retention tier (short/30d, medium/90d, long/365d) and to request custom retention with approval metadata.
3) Access events emitted to the audit log stream for every raw-telemetry read/export, containing principal, action, tenant, dataset, time range, and request-id.
4) RBAC enforcement: only allowed roles can request raw exports; UI shows redaction status on dataset views.
5) Backfill run that marks existing traces as redaction-reviewed when safe masks/hashes are applied (migration plan included).
6) Unit/integration tests covering central redaction rules, retention policy enforcement, and access-log generation.

Design notes / Implementation approach:
- Tracing redaction hooks: a lightweight interceptor added to the ingestion gateway (traces proxy). Hook uses a precedence-ordered rule set: exact allowlist attributes (pass-through) -> denylist regex -> hashing transform -> remove. Rules are tenant-configurable with per-tenant overrides.
- Patterns stored in config service; schema: list of {pattern, action, priority}. For rollout, default company-wide rule set enforced for all tenants.
- Retention enforcement: retention policy enforced at the pipeline cut-point before batching to TS/long-term store. Policies applied per-tenant at ingestion metadata tagging and then enforced periodically by retention job to drop/expiry-mark segments.
- Access logging: extend existing audit event stream (kafka) with telemetry-access events; events are immutable and stored in an append-only index with a 7-year retention for audit-only datasets.
- RBAC integration: reuse existing IAM roles from console; add granular permissions telemetry:read:raw, telemetry:manage-retention.
- Observability: new dashboards showing redaction_hits, retention_overrides, access_log_rate, and unauthorized-access_attempts by tenant. Include alerting for redaction rule surges and unexpected drop in redaction_hits.

Data privacy & compliance considerations:
- All transformations are irreversible by default (hashing with tenant-specific salt stored in KMS).
- Admins can request a supervised unmask for legal reasons; this flow requires recorded justification and approval (out of scope for this ticket, but hooks added to support it later).

Migration plan:
1) Deploy redaction hooks in read-only mode for 2 weeks (scan-only, emit events) to measure candidate matches and false positives.
2) Run a dry-run migration: generate hashed variants for traces and store alongside originals with a migration tag.
3) After validation, flip to enforce mode and prune originals per retention rules.
4) Notify customers via release notes and console banner 1 week prior.

Rollout plan:
- Canary (5% tenants) with enforcement off but audit events on (2 weeks)
- Canary enforcement on for non-enterprise tenants (1 week)
- Gradual ramp to all tenants with telemetry monitoring and rollback flag.

Monitoring & Testing:
- Simulate high-cardinality traces in staging; measure redaction latency overhead (target < 10ms added).
- Add integration tests for rule engine with representative inputs.
- Dashboard alerts: if redaction latency >50ms for >1% of requests, auto-roll back for canary.

Dependencies:
- IAM RBAC extensions (ticket ENG-15011)
- Config service schema change (ENG-15230)
- Audit log storage capacity increase (infra-ops request INFRA-201)

Stakeholders:
- Product: Priya Raman
- Design/Console: Lena Ho
- Legal/Compliance: Marcus Green
- SRE/Infra: Sonia Patel

Deliverables / Files expected:
- Trace hook library + tests (pkg/telemetry/redactor)
- Console API + UI components for retention + audit viewer
- Retention enforcement job and migration scripts
- Dashboards and alert rules

Notes on constraints:
- Must avoid introducing any path that can leak unhashed PII in logs. All debug logging in hooks must scrub sensitive fields.
- Performance is first-class: avoid heavy regex for every span attribute; use compiled patterns and short-circuit pass-throughs for known safe attributes.

notes: This ticket deliberately avoids changing long-term archival storage format. Follow-ups will address cold-tiering and encrypted-at-rest audit retention policies.
